hero.title: Build your team abroad, without guessing who to trust
hero.subtitle: SilkHire connects companies in Georgia with vetted outsourcing agencies and freelancers in India and the Philippines. We check the legal entity, the references and the English before an agency appears in the directory.

howItWorks.title: Three steps, about four weeks
howItWorks.subtitle: You describe the work. We shortlist. You choose and sign directly with the agency.

brief.title: Tell us what you need
brief.body: One short brief: the roles, the headcount, the budget and when you want to start. It takes about five minutes and there is no charge.

shortlist.title: Get a shortlist in five days
shortlist.body: We match your brief against vetted agencies and send you three to five that genuinely fit — with rates, references and time-zone overlap already confirmed.

start.title: Meet, choose, start
start.body: You interview the shortlist and sign directly with the agency you pick. We stay involved through onboarding and check in through the first quarter.

trust.title: Why the directory is short
trust.subtitle: We turn down most agencies that apply. Every listing has cleared the same five checks, and we re-run them once a year.

legal-entity.title: Legal entity verified
legal-entity.body: We confirm the company is registered where it says it is, and that the person signing has authority to sign.

client-references.title: Client references checked
client-references.body: We speak to two current clients directly — not a testimonial page — and ask what went wrong, not just what went well.

english-interview.title: English interview passed
english-interview.body: A live call with the people who would actually work on your account, rated against the level the agency claims.

security-review.title: Security review completed
security-review.body: Data handling, access control and any certifications are reviewed before an agency can take regulated or financial work.

sample-work.title: Sample work reviewed
sample-work.body: Real deliverables from a real engagement, reviewed by someone who does that work for a living.

hero.eyebrow: For agencies in India and the Philippines
hero.title: Reach Georgian companies that are ready to hire
hero.subtitle: SilkHire is a small, vetted directory — not a bidding platform. Georgian businesses come to us with a signed-off budget and a start date, and we introduce them to three to five agencies that genuinely fit.

qualified.title: Qualified briefs only
qualified.body: Every brief has a named company, a budget range and a start date before it reaches you. No open bidding, no race to the bottom.

direct.title: You contract directly
direct.body: We introduce, then step aside. The contract is between you and the client, on your paper, at your rates.

market.title: An underserved market
market.body: Georgian companies are actively looking offshore and most of them have never worked with an agency in your country. Being early matters.

short.title: A short list, deliberately
short.body: We reject most applicants. That is what makes an introduction from us worth taking, and it is why we cannot promise to accept yours.

apply.title: Apply
apply.body: The form below, about ten minutes. We reply within five working days either way.

verify.title: Verification
verify.body: Registration documents, two client references we call ourselves, a live English interview and a security review.

publish.title: Listing goes live
publish.body: We write your profile in Georgian and English, you approve it, and it publishes. Briefs start arriving from the next matching cycle.

requirements.title: What we look for
items: A registered legal entity in India or the Philippines, trading for at least two years
At least five full-time staff on payroll, not a contractor network
Two contactable clients who will speak to us on a call
Working hours with at least four hours of overlap with a Tbilisi business day
Written English at a professional level across the team that faces clients

pricing.title: What it costs
pricing.body: Listing is free during our first year. After that, agencies pay a flat annual fee — never a percentage of your contract, and never a fee that affects where you appear in the directory.

forAgencies.formSubtitle: Ten minutes, and a reply within five working days.

hero.title: From brief to signed contract
hero.subtitle: This is the whole process, including the parts that take longer than anyone would like.

brief.title: You send a brief
brief.body: Roles, headcount, budget range, start date and anything unusual about the work. Five minutes. We may come back with two or three clarifying questions.

match.title: We match and shortlist
match.body: We check availability with agencies that fit, confirm they can actually staff your roles at your budget, and send you three to five profiles with indicative rates.

meet.title: You meet the shortlist
meet.body: Calls with the people who would run your account — not a sales team. We sit in if you want a second pair of ears, and we share a written comparison afterwards.

pilot.title: Pilot or trial period
pilot.body: Most clients start with a small paid pilot: one or two people, four to six weeks, a clearly defined deliverable. It is the cheapest way to find out whether a team fits.

sign.title: Contract and onboarding
sign.body: You sign directly with the agency. We review the contract terms with you, flag anything unusual, and stay on the onboarding calls for the first month.

after.title: Quarterly check-ins
after.body: We check in at 30, 90 and 180 days. If something is not working, we help you fix it or help you move — at no extra cost.

cost.question: What does this cost me as a client?
cost.answer: Nothing. There is no fee for a brief, a shortlist or an introduction. Agencies pay an annual listing fee, which is how the business works. We never take a percentage of your contract, because a percentage would give us a reason to push you towards the more expensive team.

contract.question: Who do I sign a contract with?
contract.answer: Directly with the agency. SilkHire is not a party to it. We will read the draft with you and point out terms that commonly cause trouble — notice periods, IP assignment, data processing — but the relationship is yours.

small.question: We only need one person. Is that too small?
small.answer: No. Several agencies in the directory take engagements starting at one person or 40 hours a month. Say so in the brief and we will shortlist accordingly.

language.question: Does the team need to speak Georgian?
language.answer: None of them do, and that is worth planning around. Offshore teams work in English, so at least one person on your side needs to be comfortable running the relationship in English. For customer-facing work in Georgian, an offshore team is the wrong tool.

timezone.question: How much overlap will we actually get?
timezone.answer: Indian teams typically share about eight hours with a Tbilisi working day, which is close to full overlap. Philippine teams share around five hours, usually your morning and their afternoon. Both work; they just need different meeting habits.

quality.question: What happens if the team underperforms?
quality.answer: Tell us early. We help you raise it with the agency and, if it does not improve, we shortlist replacements at no charge. This is exactly why we recommend starting with a paid pilot rather than a twelve-month commitment.

data.question: Can we send them customer or financial data?
data.answer: Depends on the agency and the data. Listings show which certifications an agency holds and whether it has passed our security review. For anything involving personal data, you will need a data processing agreement — we can point you at a template.

cta.title: Ready to start?
cta.body: Send a brief and we will come back within five working days.

hero.title: A directory built for one market
hero.subtitle: SilkHire exists because hiring an offshore team from Georgia is harder than it should be — not because the teams are not there, but because there is no reliable way to tell which ones are real.

story.title: Why we built it
story.body:
Georgian companies have been outsourcing for years — quietly, through personal referrals and lucky guesses. The global freelance marketplaces are built for buyers in London and New York; they assume budgets, contract norms and payment rails that do not match how a company in Tbilisi actually works.

Meanwhile the strongest agencies in India and the Philippines are not on those platforms at all. They grow through referral and they do not bid on public listings. If you are in Georgia, you have no way of reaching them.

SilkHire is the introduction layer. We do the verification once, properly, and reuse it for everyone. Georgian companies get a shortlist they can trust. Agencies get briefs with a real budget attached.

paid.title: Agencies pay, clients do not
paid.body: A flat annual listing fee. No percentage of your contract, no success fee, no referral cut — because any of those would give us a reason to steer you towards the more expensive option.

ranking.title: Nobody can buy a ranking
ranking.body: The directory sorts by fit and nothing else. There are no promoted listings, no sponsored placements, and no way to pay to skip a vetting check.

rejection.title: We say no often
rejection.body: Most applications are rejected. A directory of everyone is a directory of no one, and the whole value here is that the list is short.

direct.title: We step out of the way
direct.body: You contract directly with the agency. We are not a middleman on the invoice, and we do not mark up anyone's rates.

cta.title: Questions about any of this?
cta.body: We would rather answer them before you commit to anything.
